title: Batching Concierge: workload fingerprinting and safety-guarded continuous apply
creator: Priya Menon
description:
Goal: Build a 'Batching Concierge' service that continuously profiles production workload signatures, synthesizes workload-specific batching + caching parameter recommendations, and safely applies them via staged shadow/canary rollouts with automated rollback on signal breaches.

Scope:
- Telemetry collector for per-customer request signatures (sequence length distribution, prompt-prefix reuse, KV cache hit patterns, model variant).
- Fingerprint store and delta detection to know when an existing recommendation is stale.
- Heuristic engine that proposes parameter bundles (microbatch size, max_batch_latency_ms, cache-ttl, kv-window) tuned for cost vs latency.
- Safety fences and a staged apply pipeline: shadow-run -> canary (1%) -> ramp (10/30/100) with automatic rollback triggers.
- Console integration: UI for reviewing recommendations, accepting changes, and quick rollback.
- Audit trail for compliance (who approved, which signals triggered rollback).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline can generate and apply a recommendation for a synthetic workload in staging with a shadow-run and canary deploy.
- Define and enforce rollback thresholds: p95 latency increase <= +5ms, error rate increase <= +0.2%, quality regression (eval prompts) <= 0.5% delta, and cost reduction >= 5% to validate apply.
- Recommendations show a measurable cost delta in the cost dashboard and include an explainability comment (why these parameters).
- Console shows per-customer preview and approval flow.

Non-goals: autonomous global forced apply without explicit canary/approval, deeper model tuning (left to model team), or replacing manual SRE overrides for emergency incidents.
comments: 2025-09-11 - Kickoff: design review with PM (Jordan Lee) and Design (Marta Novak). Agreed telemetry schema and sample sizes for fingerprints. Action: Evan to prototype collector + store in staging.

2025-09-15 - Prototype update: simple sketch stores (seq_len_hist, prefix_hashes, kv_reuse_rate) in Dynamo. Early findings: 22% of traffic has prefix reuse > 0.3 which suggests benefit from prefix caching for those tenants.

2025-09-18 - Trade-off discussion: conservative vs aggressive batching. Decided to prefer conservative defaults for first rollouts (smaller microbatch increments) and add a tuning knob per customer tier. Documented in Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/BC-Concierge-Design

2025-09-20 - Security review checklist added by Security (Anita Bose): ensure PII strip before telemetry, KMS for fingerprint store. Marked security_review_required=false for this ticket because controls will be implemented as separate tasks (see ENG-215100).

2025-09-21 - Data science note (Tomás Rivera): created synthetic evaluation set for quality regressions and integrated it into the canary pipeline. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124

2025-09-22 - Implementation progress: shadow-run framework in runtime has a stubbed hook; batching heuristic engine MVP committed in branch 'batching/concierge-mvp'. Benchmarks show initial cost reduction estimate ~6% for target cohort, p95 latency impact +2ms. Link to perf dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/batching/concierge-signals?project=cost-opt

2025-09-24 - Code review feedback (PM + SRE): add a circuit-breaker that prevents ramp if underlying infra error rate > 0.5% and add an offline 'dry-apply' mode for manual verification. Evan pushed changes in PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/88

2025-09-25 - Next steps: 1) Run a 7-day shadow experiment across 3 customer cohorts (low/medium/high prefix reuse). 2) Implement UI approval flow and audit logging (design tickets: DES-7124). 3) Wire rollback webhook to Incident Commander runbook (runbook: https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/batching-concierge).
